title: Bounded Autonomy: Limits, Permissions and Sandboxes
summary: The more an agent can do on its own, the more it can get wrong on its own. This lesson shows how to give agents exactly as much freedom as their reliability justifies: hard limits, permission tiers, human approval where it pays, sandboxed execution and a capped blast radius.
objectives: After this lesson you can frame autonomy as expected loss: probability of error times impact, and use it to decide what needs approval
Set step, token, cost and time limits from the measured distribution of normal runs
Design permission tiers and a tool policy enforced in code, not in the prompt
Estimate how layered defences combine and why independence matters
Bound the worst case with rate limits, sandboxes and kill switches, and test these in the support-agent sandbox
prerequisites: Failure handling from [/learn/agents/failures-and-recovery](/learn/agents/failures-and-recovery), traces and evaluation from [/learn/agents/traces-and-evaluation](/learn/agents/traces-and-evaluation), and tool security issues from [/learn/agents/tools-and-mcp](/learn/agents/tools-and-mcp). Prompt injection is covered in [/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-injection](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-injection).
